insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic attribution. This protocol settles verified purchase events at ~$0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost difference rooted in structure, not negotiation: the receipt eliminates the attribution problem rather than solving it.

Cookies are gone, device fingerprinting is degrading, and first-party data stops at your own ecosystem boundary. Verified, identity-free receipt signals are one of the few remaining mechanisms that confirm a purchase actually occurred — without requiring identity attachment.

Amazon knows what you buy on Amazon. Walmart knows what you buy at Walmart. Neither sees the full wallet. At 5,071 verified receipts across brick-and-mortar, grocery, pharmacy, and online channels, this dataset reflects cross-ecosystem purchase behavior that no single retailer can observe internally.

78%+ of receipts in the current 14-day window are brick-and-mortar — restaurants, grocery, gas, retail. This is the commerce that digital ad targeting has always struggled to attribute. The signal is strongest precisely where cookies were weakest.

insights.topic: Data quality ceiling at merchant resolution
insights.insight: 11% of receipts currently fail merchant classification, landing in an 'Unknown' bucket with a $290 average transaction — likely high-ticket or B2B. Cross-domain purchase analysis should be treated as an inference until resolution improves, not a confirmed signal.

Token velocity dropped week-over-week (0.694x) while acceleration held above 1.0x. That divergence — fewer receipts per cycle but a stable growth trend line — suggests durable adoption rather than a promotional spike. Brands evaluating this data source should weight trend slope over weekly volume.
